title: Officials’ own property next to a City deal
question: Did an official who sponsored, voted on or worked on a City property deal declare an interest in property within 150 metres of it?
finding: Across 228 City purchases, leases, loans and sales with a known address, 1 pairing with an official’s declared property within 150 metres turned up, involving 1 official; 0 sponsored the file. The nearest is Aaron Peskin (supervisor), who declared property on the 500 block of Filbert Street, 93 metres from 777 Broadway Street, 1525 Grant Avenue, 1207 Mason Street (city housing loan, 2022).
how: Addresses that officials wrote on Form 700 Schedule B (real property other than a home they live in), matched to the City address table and measured against each deal’s address. Only annual and leaving-office statements whose period covers the date the Board file was introduced are used. The declared property is shown only to the block.
limits: 4,726 of the 5,731 San Francisco properties on annual and leaving-office statements could be placed on the map; the rest are written too loosely to match. This is a proximity lead and nothing more. Owning property near a City project is common in a seven-mile-square city; the conflict rules turn on whether a decision would materially affect the property’s value and whether the official took part, which no dataset records. The Board data shows sponsors, not who voted or who abstained. Board and Mayor’s Office entries include staff as well as elected officials. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

rows.deal: 777 Broadway Street, 1525 Grant Avenue, 1207 Mason Street
rows.link: At the Board of Supervisors (member or staff) when it was approved
